title: Make bad rate-limit configuration fail at load

blocks.text: The API gateway reads its rate limits from a YAML file: for each route, a list of requests allowed per minute, one per customer tier. Last week someone wrote a limit as `"20"`, in quotes. The gateway started without a complaint, and the first request to that route killed the request scheduler with a `ClassCastException` in code that has no cast. On another night, a hot-reload job edited the parsed tree after it was loaded, and the running limits changed under the scheduler.
`RateLimits` already loads the file. Finish the `TODO` in `src/main/java/practice/RateLimits.java`:

items: `integers(route, node)`: turn one route's parsed node into the list of limits the rest of the gateway reads.

blocks.text: When you're done, bad configuration stops the load itself, with an `IllegalArgumentException` whose message names the route, and the limits a `RateLimits` holds can't change after `load` returns. The method needs no `@SuppressWarnings`. About ten lines in total.

cases.says: well-formed limits load, and each route and tier reads its own value
a route whose node isn't a list is refused at load, and the message names the route
a list that holds a string is refused at load, not at the first read of the limit
every element is checked, so a bad limit after good ones is refused too
a change to the parsed list after load reaches neither the limits nor their checks

origin.section: @SuppressWarnings Covers Its Whole Declaration, Including Warnings Added Later

concepts: A cast to a parameterized type checks only the class, so code that converts untyped input checks each element and needs no suppression; otherwise the ClassCastException comes later, at a read with no cast.
